assessment: The incumbent appears useful for routine weeks: unchanged-assignment centers had seven-minute median handling, although that subgroup does not establish causality. Overall course-set accuracy was 32/40 and median handling was 17 minutes, below the desired performance. Assignment changes concentrate among affected exports, making requested-week semantics a plausible weakness. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. No observed cross-center rows is reassuring only for the sampled cases; the split-course center was absent. Any bounded change must retain private authorized processing, the documented CSV, concurrent attendance entry, six engineer-days and the hosting allowance. Supplied synthetic observations support hypotheses, not implementation conclusions.

openings.claim: Selecting requested-week courses through current assignments or mutable names may create apparent or actual omissions; stable course identity and week-relevant membership may resolve different portions of the problem.
openings.delta: Distinguish historical membership errors from naming mismatches before choosing a correction.
openings.prediction: With intended course identities fixed, assignment-only changes affect exported membership if temporal selection is responsible; rename-only changes preserve identities but alter coordinator recognition if naming is responsible.
openings.probe: In private staging, vary fabricated assignment changes and renames independently against an agreed weekly course set. Compare exported identities and coordinator judgments, retaining the CSV schema. Include a split-course fixture with distinct centers and attendance entry during export. Estimate any repair before committing the six-day budget.
assumptions: Staging can represent these transitions within existing resources.
Historical assignment data availability is unknown; a repair depending on it remains conditional.

openings.claim: Does active checking or correction dominate coordinator handling, or does replacement-file retrieval consume enough active work to explain the target gap?
openings.delta: Separate active labor from elapsed replacement delay; job duration alone measures neither.
openings.prediction: A retrieval bottleneck yields substantial active request, follow-up and download time; a checking bottleneck yields substantial schedule comparison or spreadsheet correction despite prompt file availability.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions with each consenting coordinator for fabricated routine and changed-course exports. Record active minutes by checking, correcting, requesting, downloading and importing; record waiting separately. Compare the dominant components and disagreements between course references.
assumptions: Fabricated sessions approximate ordinary workflow sufficiently to identify a candidate bottleneck.
Session findings cannot establish success across the next 40 exports.
